Definition: from G1223 and a derivative of the base of G4008; to cross entirely:--go over, pass (over), sail over.
BiblicalUsage: To pass over is to cross from one shore to another, and the word is used of boats, of crowds, and of the gulf no man can cross. Jesus passes over the sea to His own city, He comes to the land of Gennesaret, Paul's ship passes over to Phoenicia, and Abraham tells the rich man that none may pass from torment to comfort.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the crossings in the Gospels show who Jesus is. He crosses seas the disciples fear, He crosses into the country of the Gerasenes to free one man, and the gulf He cannot cross is the one sin fixed between the lost and God.
